title: 未必 / 不見得 — 'not necessarily'
pattern: 未必 / 不見得 / 不一定 + V/Adj
explanation: All mean 'not necessarily'. 不見得 is the natural spoken choice in Taiwan and can stand alone as a reply; 未必 is neutral-to-written; 不一定 also covers 'it depends'. They politely challenge a generalization.
contrast: Learners default to 不一定 for everything. Standalone 那可不見得 / 那可未必 has a mainland ring; in Taiwan say 不見得吧.

examples.zh: 貴的東西不見得比較好用。
examples.en: Expensive things aren't necessarily better to use.

examples.zh: 他說的未必是真的，你再查一下。
examples.en: What he said isn't necessarily true; check again.

examples.zh: 學歷高不見得就找得到好工作。
examples.en: A high degree doesn't necessarily land you a good job.

examples.zh: 這樣做未必能解決問題。
examples.en: Doing this won't necessarily solve the problem.

practice.en: Rich people aren't necessarily happy.
practice.zh: 有錢人不見得快樂。

practice.en: The newest phone isn't necessarily the best.
practice.zh: 最新的手機未必是最好的。

title: 給 + 人 + V — 'let someone V' and other Taiwanese-style 給
pattern: 給 + person + V ; 你給我 + V！
explanation: Influenced by Taiwanese hōo, 給 can mean 'let / allow' (給他等 'let him wait', 給我看一下 'let me see') and, more colloquially, mark the person you suffer something from (給人家笑 'get laughed at'). 你給我 + V is a stern command. Colloquial; in careful speech 讓 replaces it.
contrast: Mainland/textbook: 讓他等 / 讓我看一下 / 被人笑. Learners know 給 only as 'give' or 'for'; in Taiwan 給我看 is 'let me see'.

examples.zh: 沒關係，給他等一下又不會怎樣。
examples.en: It's fine; letting him wait a bit won't hurt.

examples.zh: 手機借我，給我看一下那張照片。
examples.en: Lend me your phone and let me see that photo.

examples.zh: 你這樣穿出去會給人家笑。
examples.en: You'll get laughed at if you go out dressed like that.

examples.zh: 你給我過來，把話講清楚！
examples.en: Get over here and explain yourself!

practice.en: Let me think about it for a bit.
practice.zh: 給我想一下。

practice.en: Don't let the kid play on the phone for too long.
practice.zh: 不要給小孩玩手機玩太久。

title: 儘管…還是 — 'even though / despite' and 'feel free to'
pattern: 儘管 + fact，(S) 還是/仍然/卻 + result ; 儘管 + V (imperative)
explanation: 儘管 concedes a real fact more emphatically than 雖然; the second clause takes 還是, 仍然, 依然 or 卻. In invitations, 儘管 + V means 'feel free to' (有問題儘管問).
contrast: Write 儘管 (not 盡管) in Taiwan — simplified script merges 儘 and 盡 into one character, so converted text is often wrong. Don't confuse it with hypothetical 就算.

examples.zh: 儘管下著大雨，他還是準時到了。
examples.en: Despite the heavy rain, he still arrived on time.

examples.zh: 儘管大家都反對，她仍然堅持要去。
examples.en: Even though everyone objected, she still insisted on going.

examples.zh: 有什麼問題儘管問，不用客氣。
examples.en: If you have any questions, feel free to ask; don't be shy.

practice.en: Although he was very tired, he still finished the work.
practice.zh: 儘管很累，他還是把工作做完了。

practice.en: If you need help, feel free to tell me.
practice.zh: 需要幫忙的話，儘管跟我說。

title: 尚未 / 尚 / 仍 / 已 / 曾 — one-syllable formal adverbs
pattern: 尚未 + V (= 還沒) ; 尚 (= 還) ; 仍 (= 還是) ; 已 (= 已經) ; 曾 (= 曾經)
explanation: Formal writing compresses time adverbs to one syllable: 已 (已經), 仍 (仍然 / 還), 尚 (還), 尚未 (還沒), 曾 (曾經), 未 (沒有). News leads rely on them: 已完成, 仍在調查, 尚未決定.
contrast: Spoken: 已經 / 還 / 還沒. Slipping 還沒 into a formal report weakens the register; conversely 尚未 in speech sounds like reading a statement.

examples.zh: 事故原因尚未查明，警方仍在調查。
examples.en: The cause of the accident has not yet been determined; police are still investigating.

examples.zh: 相關法案已送交立法院審議。
examples.en: The relevant bill has been sent to the Legislative Yuan for review.

examples.zh: 目前疫情尚屬穩定，民眾不必恐慌。
examples.en: The outbreak is still stable for now; there is no need for the public to panic.

examples.zh: 他曾在國外工作多年。
examples.en: He once worked abroad for many years.

practice.en: The date of the meeting has not yet been decided.
practice.zh: 會議日期尚未決定。

practice.en: That section of road is still closed.
practice.zh: 該路段目前仍封閉中。

title: V + 說 — 說 as 'that' (complementizer)
pattern: 覺得 / 想 / 以為 / 擔心 / 變成 + 說 + clause
explanation: After verbs of thinking, saying and feeling, Taiwanese often insert 說 before the clause, much like English 'that': 我覺得說…, 他以為說…, 變成說…. It carries no meaning of speaking; it buys planning time and signals that a full clause follows. Spoken only — never write it in essays.
contrast: Mainland/textbook: 我覺得… directly, with no 說. Don't translate it, and don't use it in every clause — that sounds rambling.

examples.zh: 我覺得說，這件事還是當面講比較好。
examples.en: I feel that this is still better discussed face to face.

examples.zh: 他以為說我們已經出發了。
examples.en: He thought that we had already set off.

examples.zh: 後來就變成說，每個人都要加班。
examples.en: And then it ended up that everybody had to work overtime.

examples.zh: 我是擔心說時間會來不及。
examples.en: I'm just worried that there won't be enough time.

practice.en: I feel that it's a bit too expensive.
practice.zh: 我覺得說有點太貴了。

practice.en: She thought that you didn't like her.
practice.zh: 她以為說你不喜歡她。

title: 咧 — casual 呢, teasing emphasis
pattern: N + 咧？ ; 然後咧？ ; 才怪咧 ; 還…咧
explanation: 咧 is the casual Taiwan counterpart of 呢 in follow-up questions (你咧？ 然後咧？) and 'where is…?' questions (我的筆咧？). After denials it adds a teasing punch (才怪咧), and 還…咧 mocks a claim ('and you said…').
contrast: Mainland/textbook: 你呢？/ 然後呢？/ 才怪呢. Minimal pair: 你呢？ (neutral) vs 你咧？ (casual, local). Avoid 咧 in formal settings.

examples.zh: 我吃飽了，你咧？
examples.en: I'm full. What about you?

examples.zh: 然後咧？他後來怎麼說？
examples.en: And then? What did he say after that?

examples.zh: 我的悠遊卡咧？剛剛還在啊。
examples.en: Where's my EasyCard? It was just here.

examples.zh: 還說要早起咧，結果睡到中午。
examples.en: And you said you'd get up early — you slept till noon.

practice.en: I'm having noodles. What about you?
practice.zh: 我要吃麵，你咧？

practice.en: Where's my phone?
practice.zh: 我的手機咧？

title: 基本上 / 老實說 / 說真的 — stance openers
pattern: 基本上，… ; 老實說 / 說真的 / 坦白講，…
explanation: 基本上 hedges a generalization ('basically, for the most part') and is a favorite of Taiwanese office and interview speech. 老實說, 說真的 and 坦白講 announce a candid opinion, usually a negative one, and cushion it. They buy thinking time and signal what kind of statement is coming.
contrast: Mainland: 說實話 / 講真 / 實話實說. 說實話 is understood; 老實說 and 說真的 are more common in Taiwan.

examples.zh: 基本上我都在家煮，很少叫外送。
examples.en: For the most part I cook at home; I rarely order delivery.

examples.zh: 基本上沒什麼問題，細節再調整就好。
examples.en: Basically there's no problem; we just need to adjust the details.

examples.zh: 老實說，我覺得這個價錢太高了。
examples.en: Honestly, I think this price is too high.

examples.zh: 說真的，你不用太在意別人怎麼看。
examples.en: Seriously, you don't need to care so much about what others think.

practice.en: Basically, I agree with you.
practice.zh: 基本上我同意你的看法。

practice.en: To be honest, I didn't really understand it.
practice.zh: 老實說，我不太懂。

title: 至於 / 不至於 — 'as for' and 'not to the point of'
pattern: …。至於 + new topic，… ; (還) 不至於 + V
explanation: 至於 shifts to a related but separate item: 'as for'. It is how you set something aside to treat it separately. 不至於 means 'wouldn't go so far as to'.
contrast: The mainland retort 至於嗎？ is replaced in Taiwan by 有需要這樣嗎？/ 有這麼誇張嗎？ Don't open a brand-new topic with 至於 (use 關於).

examples.zh: 機票我來訂，至於住宿就交給你了。
examples.en: I'll book the flights; as for accommodation, I'll leave that to you.

examples.zh: 我只負責設計，至於價錢要問老闆。
examples.en: I only handle the design; as for the price, you'll have to ask the boss.

examples.zh: 他雖然生氣，但還不至於不理你。
examples.en: He's angry, but not to the point of ignoring you.

practice.en: I'll bring the drinks. As for food, everyone brings their own.
practice.zh: 飲料我帶，至於吃的，大家自己準備。

practice.en: It's a little expensive, but not so much that I can't afford it.
practice.zh: 是有點貴，但還不至於買不起。

title: 並未 / 並非 / 並不 — emphatic formal negation
pattern: 並 + 未 / 非 / 不 / 無 + …
explanation: 並 before a negative stresses that reality differs from what was assumed: 並未 'has not in fact', 並非 'is not actually', 並不 'not at all', 並無 'there is in fact no'. A standard tool for denial and clarification in statements and essays.
contrast: Spoken: 並沒有 / 並不是 / 其實沒有. ✗ 並 without a following negative for emphasis. 並非 + noun/clause; 並不 + adjective/verb.

examples.zh: 該公司並未對此事做出回應。
examples.en: The company has not in fact responded to the matter.

examples.zh: 成功並非一朝一夕可以達成。
examples.en: Success is not something achieved overnight.

examples.zh: 調查顯示，這種說法並無根據。
examples.en: The investigation shows that this claim is groundless.

examples.zh: 事情並不像外界想的那麼簡單。
examples.en: The matter is not as simple as outsiders think.

practice.en: This is not the final decision.
practice.zh: 這並非最後的決定。

practice.en: The police did not find any suspicious items.
practice.zh: 警方並未發現任何可疑物品。

title: 關於 / 對於 / 就…而言 — 'regarding / toward / as far as … goes'
pattern: 關於 + topic ; 對於 + target of attitude ; 就 + N + 而言/來說 ; 對 + person + 來說
explanation: 關於 introduces what something is about and can modify nouns (關於…的問題). 對於 marks the target of an attitude or action. 就…而言 / 就…來說 limits the viewpoint ('as far as … is concerned'); 對…來說 is the spoken 'for (someone)'.
contrast: ✗ 對於這件事的消息 → 關於這件事的消息. A 關於-phrase can't follow the subject (✗ 我關於這件事不清楚). 就…而言 is formal; say 對…來說 in speech.

examples.zh: 關於這個問題，我們下次開會再討論。
examples.en: Regarding this issue, we'll discuss it at the next meeting.

examples.zh: 對於這次的結果，他不太滿意。
examples.en: He's not very satisfied with this result.

examples.zh: 就價格而言，這家算是很合理。
examples.en: As far as price goes, this place is quite reasonable.

examples.zh: 對我來說，通勤時間比薪水重要。
examples.en: For me, commute time matters more than salary.

practice.en: I'd like to ask a question about refunds.
practice.zh: 我想問一個關於退費的問題。

practice.en: As far as quality is concerned, this one is the best.
practice.zh: 就品質而言，這個是最好的。

title: 在那邊 + V — dismissive 'sitting there V-ing'
pattern: (還 / 一直 / 只會 / 不要) 在那邊 + V
explanation: 在那邊 (or 在那裡) before a verb has nothing to do with location: it disparages the action as pointless, annoying or pretentious. Typical with 還, 一直, 只會 and verbs like 講, 抱怨, 裝, 拖. Colloquial and critical in tone.
contrast: Mainland: 還在那兒… / 瞎… / 淨…. Learners take it literally as 'over there'; tone and context show it's a complaint.

examples.zh: 都幾點了，你還在那邊滑手機。
examples.en: Look at the time, and you're still scrolling on your phone.

examples.zh: 他只會在那邊抱怨，都不想辦法。
examples.en: All he does is complain; he never tries to find a solution.

examples.zh: 你不要在那邊亂講，我哪有說過。
examples.en: Stop making things up; I never said that.

examples.zh: 不會就問啊，不要在那邊裝懂。
examples.en: If you don't know, ask — don't pretend you understand.

practice.en: Stop making excuses.
practice.zh: 你不要在那邊找藉口。

practice.en: He just keeps dragging his feet.
practice.zh: 他一直在那邊拖。

title: 把 — beyond the basics
pattern: 把 + O + V + 成/作/在/到/給 … ; 把 + O + 給 + V 了 ; 把它 + V + 掉
explanation: 把 is required when the verb is followed by 成, 作, 在, 到 or 給 plus a second element (把 A 當成 B, 把車停在…). Colloquially 給 can be inserted before the verb for emphasis (把這件事給忘了), and Taiwanese say 把它 + V + 掉 constantly. The formal written equivalent is 將.
contrast: ✗ 我放書在桌上 → 我把書放在桌上. The verb can't be bare (✗ 把飯吃). Learners avoid 把 and produce unnatural SVO sentences.

examples.zh: 他把我當成他的親妹妹。
examples.en: He treats me as his own little sister.

examples.zh: 請把這份文件翻成英文。
examples.en: Please translate this document into English.

examples.zh: 我居然把他的生日給忘了。
examples.en: I actually went and forgot his birthday.

examples.zh: 剩下的菜你把它吃掉，不要浪費。
examples.en: Finish off the leftover dishes; don't waste them.

practice.en: Please park the car in the basement.
practice.zh: 請把車停在地下室。

practice.en: Don't treat me like a child.
practice.zh: 不要把我當成小孩子。

title: 以…為 — 'take A as B'
pattern: 以 + A + 為 + B (主 / 例 / 目標 / 基礎 / 優先 / 榮)
explanation: 以 A 為 B means 'take A as B / with A as B': 以學生為主 'mainly students', 以…為例 'take … as an example', 以…為目標. A core structure of expository writing, also heard in formal speech and presentations.
contrast: Spoken: 把 A 當作 B / 主要是 A / 拿 A 來說. 為 here is second tone (wéi). ✗ 以…做為例 is redundant.

examples.zh: 這家餐廳的客人以上班族為主。
examples.en: This restaurant's customers are mainly office workers.

examples.zh: 以台北為例，房價十年內漲了一倍。
examples.en: Take Taipei as an example: housing prices doubled within ten years.

examples.zh: 我們以顧客的需求為優先。
examples.en: We put customers' needs first.

examples.zh: 全家人都以她為榮。
examples.en: The whole family is proud of her.

practice.en: This course consists mainly of conversation practice.
practice.zh: 這門課以會話練習為主。

practice.en: Take me as an example: I commute an hour every day.
practice.zh: 以我為例，我每天通勤一個小時。

title: 被 — beyond the basics (被…給、遭、受)
pattern: 被 + (agent) + (給) + V ; 遭(到) + V ; 受(到) + V/N
explanation: 被 typically marks something unwelcome and may omit the agent (被罵了) or add colloquial 給 (被他給騙了). News prose prefers 遭 / 遭到 for harm (遭竊, 遭到拒絕) and 受 / 受到 for influence or favor (受到歡迎, 受到影響).
contrast: Mainland colloquial passives with 叫 / 讓 (我叫他騙了) are uncommon in Taiwan. Avoid 被 for neutral results where Chinese prefers a topic sentence (✗ 信被寫好了 → 信寫好了).

examples.zh: 我的腳踏車昨天被偷了。
examples.en: My bicycle was stolen yesterday.

examples.zh: 我差點被他給騙了。
examples.en: I was nearly fooled by him.

examples.zh: 他的提案遭到主管拒絕。
examples.en: His proposal was rejected by the manager.

examples.zh: 這部電影在年輕人當中很受歡迎。
examples.en: This film is very popular among young people.

practice.en: I got scolded by my boss this morning.
practice.zh: 我今天早上被老闆罵了。

practice.en: This policy has been strongly criticized.
practice.zh: 這項政策受到強烈批評。

title: 也是啦 / 是沒錯啦…可是 — conceding before disagreeing
pattern: 也是啦。 ; (這樣講) 是沒錯啦，可是/但是… ; Adj 是 Adj 啦，可是…
explanation: Taiwanese conversation avoids flat contradiction. 也是啦 grants the other person's point ('true, I guess'); 是沒錯啦…可是 concedes before raising an objection ('that's true, but…'). The 啦 makes the concession sound reluctant and friendly rather than final.
contrast: Mainland: 那倒也是 / 話是這麼說，但是…. A learner's direct 不對 or 我不同意 comes across as confrontational in Taiwan.

examples.zh: 也是啦，現在買房真的太貴了。
examples.en: True, I guess — buying a home really is too expensive now.

examples.zh: 是沒錯啦，可是我還是覺得怪怪的。
examples.en: That's true, but it still feels off to me.

examples.zh: 便宜是便宜啦，但是品質不太好。
examples.en: It is cheap, sure, but the quality isn't great.

examples.zh: 你這樣講也是啦，那再看看好了。
examples.en: You have a point there; let's wait and see then.

practice.en: That's true, but we don't have enough time.
practice.zh: 是沒錯啦，可是我們時間不夠。

practice.en: Fair enough, health is the most important thing.
practice.zh: 也是啦，身體健康最重要。

title: 進行 + N — formal 'carry out'
pattern: (對 + O) + 進行 + two-syllable action noun
explanation: 進行 followed by a two-syllable action noun is the standard formal way to describe organized activity: 進行調查, 進行討論, 進行維修. Similar light verbs: 展開 (launch), 舉行 (hold), 實施 (implement), 做出 (make: 做出決定).
contrast: Spoken: just the verb (調查 / 討論 / 修). ✗ 進行 + a casual or one-syllable verb (✗ 進行吃飯, ✗ 進行看).

examples.zh: 警方正在對這起案件進行調查。
examples.en: Police are conducting an investigation into this case.

examples.zh: 電梯進行維修，請改走樓梯。
examples.en: The elevator is under maintenance; please use the stairs.

examples.zh: 雙方將於下週進行第二次協商。
examples.en: The two sides will hold a second round of talks next week.

examples.zh: 系統將於凌晨兩點進行更新。
examples.en: The system will undergo an update at 2 a.m.

practice.en: The school will hold a fire drill tomorrow.
practice.zh: 學校明天將進行消防演習。

practice.en: We are currently testing the new system.
practice.zh: 我們目前正在對新系統進行測試。

title: 幾乎 vs 簡直 — 'almost' vs 'simply / practically'
pattern: 幾乎 + 都/每/沒/全 … ; 簡直 + 是/像/太…了/讓人…
explanation: 幾乎 is factual 'almost, nearly' and combines with totals and negatives (幾乎每天, 幾乎沒有). 簡直 is rhetorical 'simply, practically' — it exaggerates for effect and introduces a comparison or judgment (簡直像做夢).
contrast: ✗ 簡直每天都下雨 (factual → 幾乎). 差不多 is the looser spoken 'almost'. Taiwanese also use 根本 for the exaggerating sense (根本是詐騙).

examples.zh: 我幾乎每天都會經過這家店。
examples.en: I pass by this shop almost every day.

examples.zh: 這個月的薪水幾乎都花光了。
examples.en: I've spent almost all of this month's salary.

examples.zh: 這裡的風景簡直像明信片一樣。
examples.en: The scenery here is practically like a postcard.

examples.zh: 他講話的態度簡直讓人受不了。
examples.en: His attitude when he talks is simply unbearable.

practice.en: Almost nobody knew about this.
practice.zh: 這件事幾乎沒有人知道。

practice.en: That is simply impossible.
practice.zh: 這簡直是不可能的事。

title: 畢竟 — 'after all'
pattern: 畢竟 + decisive fact
explanation: 畢竟 brings in the fundamental fact that explains or excuses a situation. It can go before or after the subject and often softens criticism (他畢竟還是個孩子).
contrast: Don't use 畢竟 in questions (use 到底 / 究竟) or for 'finally' (use 終於). 終究 is a more literary relative meaning 'in the end'.

examples.zh: 不要太苛責他，畢竟他才剛來。
examples.en: Don't be too hard on him; after all, he just got here.

examples.zh: 畢竟是自己的選擇，再累也要撐下去。
examples.en: It was my own choice after all, so I have to hang in there however tiring.

examples.zh: 我們畢竟認識十年了，我很瞭解他。
examples.en: We've known each other ten years, after all; I know him well.

practice.en: Listen to her; after all, she has more experience.
practice.zh: 聽她的吧，畢竟她比較有經驗。

practice.en: After all, health is what matters most.
practice.zh: 畢竟健康才是最重要的。

title: 講 / 說 / 提 / 聊 — choosing the right 'say'
pattern: 講/說 + content ; 講話 / 講電話 ; 提(到) + topic ; 聊 + topic
explanation: 講 and 說 both mean 'say / speak'; Taiwan speech favors 講 (講話, 講電話, 亂講, 講不聽), while 說 stays in quoting and set words (聽說, 說不定, 說明). 提 / 提到 means 'bring up, mention' without detail; 聊 is 'chat about'. 講 also means 'explain' (老師講得很清楚).
contrast: Mainland speech defaults to 說 (說話, 打電話, 瞎說). Learners trained on 說 sound more Taiwanese simply by switching to 講 in casual talk. ✗ 提 + a full quotation.

examples.zh: 他在講電話，你等一下再找他。
examples.en: He's on the phone; look for him later.

examples.zh: 你上次提到的那家店叫什麼？
examples.en: What's the name of that shop you mentioned last time?

examples.zh: 我們聊了一個晚上，聊到店都要關了。
examples.en: We chatted the whole evening, until the shop was about to close.

examples.zh: 你不要亂講，他聽到會生氣。
examples.en: Don't talk nonsense; he'll be mad if he hears it.

practice.en: She never mentioned this to me.
practice.zh: 她從來沒有跟我提過這件事。

practice.en: Can you say it again? I didn't hear clearly.
practice.zh: 你可以再講一次嗎？我沒聽清楚。

title: 據…表示 / 指出 — attributing information
pattern: 據 + source + 表示/指出/報導/統計/瞭解，… ; source + 表示/指出/強調/呼籲，…
explanation: News style attributes information with 據…: 據報導 'reportedly', 據統計 'according to statistics', 據瞭解 'it is understood that'. Speakers are quoted with 表示 (stated), 指出 (pointed out), 強調 (stressed), 坦言 (admitted) or 呼籲 (urged) rather than 說.
contrast: Spoken: 聽說 / 他說. ✗ 根據他表示 → 據他表示 / 根據他的說法. Repeating 說 throughout an essay reads as immature.

examples.zh: 據氣象署表示，本週末將有寒流來襲。
examples.en: According to the weather administration, a cold wave will hit this weekend.

examples.zh: 專家指出，睡眠不足會影響記憶力。
examples.en: Experts point out that lack of sleep affects memory.

examples.zh: 據統計，台灣每年有超過一千萬人次出國。
examples.en: Statistics show that people in Taiwan make over ten million trips abroad each year.

examples.zh: 市長強調，絕不會調漲捷運票價。
examples.en: The mayor stressed that MRT fares will absolutely not be raised.

practice.en: According to reports, the accident injured three people.
practice.zh: 據報導，這起事故造成三人受傷。

practice.en: Doctors urge the public to get vaccinated early.
practice.zh: 醫師呼籲民眾儘早接種疫苗。

title: 偏偏 — 'of all things / it just had to'
pattern: 偏偏 + clause ; S + 偏偏 + V ; 偏要 / 偏不
explanation: 偏偏 says that reality perversely goes against what one wants ('of all times…', 'it just had to…') or that someone willfully does the opposite of what they're told (偏要, 偏不). It carries frustration.
contrast: Learners use 但是 and lose the 'just my luck' feeling. Mainland 偏生 / 偏巧 aren't used in Taiwan.

examples.zh: 我趕時間，偏偏遇到大塞車。
examples.en: I was in a hurry, and of all things I hit a huge traffic jam.

examples.zh: 平常都沒事，偏偏今天電腦壞了。
examples.en: It's normally fine, but the computer just had to break today.

examples.zh: 叫他不要去，他偏要去。
examples.en: I told him not to go, but he insists on going.

examples.zh: 這麼多人，為什麼偏偏選我？
examples.en: With so many people, why pick me of all people?

practice.en: I wanted to sleep in, but the neighbors just had to start renovating.
practice.zh: 我想睡晚一點，偏偏鄰居在裝潢。

practice.en: I told her not to buy it, but she insisted on buying it.
practice.zh: 我叫她不要買，她偏要買。

title: 呢 — what Taiwan keeps and what it drops
pattern: N + 呢？ ; wh-question + 呢？ ; (✗ 在 V 呢 / 還沒 V 呢)
explanation: Taiwanese use 呢 mainly in follow-up questions (那你呢？) and to make wh-questions sound thoughtful or polite (該怎麼辦呢？), which gives it a gentle, slightly written feel. The northern uses for ongoing action or emphasis (他正吃飯呢, 還早呢) are uncommon; Taiwan uses 在 + V, 還 or 耶 / 啊 instead.
contrast: Mainland/textbook: 他在睡覺呢 / 我還沒吃呢 / 可好吃呢. In Taiwan: 他在睡覺 / 我還沒吃 / 很好吃耶. Minimal pair: 怎麼辦？ (urgent) vs 怎麼辦呢？ (musing, softer).

examples.zh: 我要點珍奶，那你呢？
examples.en: I'm getting bubble tea — what about you?

examples.zh: 這麼多東西，要怎麼帶回去呢？
examples.en: With this much stuff, how are we going to carry it back?

examples.zh: 請問您要找哪一位呢？
examples.en: May I ask who you're looking for?

examples.zh: 他還在睡覺，你晚點再打來。
examples.en: He's still asleep; call again later. (no 呢, the Taiwan way)

practice.en: I like summer. And you?
practice.zh: 我喜歡夏天，你呢？

practice.en: I haven't eaten yet. (Taiwan style, without 呢)
practice.zh: 我還沒吃。

title: 對了 / 話說 / 話說回來 — steering the topic
pattern: 對了，… ; 話說，… ; 話說回來，…
explanation: 對了 introduces something you just remembered ('oh, by the way'). 話說 opens a new or loosely related topic ('so, speaking of which'), common in chat and online posts. 話說回來 returns to the main point or adds a balancing view ('that said').
contrast: Mainland: 話又說回來 / 說起來. 順便說一下 is a literal translation of 'by the way' and sounds stiff; use 對了.

examples.zh: 對了，你上次說的那本書叫什麼？
examples.en: Oh, by the way, what was that book you mentioned last time?

examples.zh: 話說，你後來有去面試嗎？
examples.en: So, did you end up going to the interview?

examples.zh: 話說回來，他也不是故意的。
examples.en: That said, he didn't do it on purpose.

examples.zh: 對了，明天記得帶健保卡。
examples.en: Oh right — remember to bring your health insurance card tomorrow.

practice.en: By the way, have you booked the hotel yet?
practice.zh: 對了，你訂飯店了沒？

practice.en: That said, the price really is reasonable.
practice.zh: 話說回來，價錢真的很合理。

title: 乾脆 — 'might as well just'
pattern: (那 / 不然) 乾脆 + VP (+ 好了 / 算了)
explanation: 乾脆 proposes the simplest, most decisive option after the alternatives look troublesome: 'might as well just…'. It often pairs with 好了 or 算了. As an adjective it describes someone decisive and straightforward (他很乾脆).
contrast: Mainland alternatives are 索性 (written) and northern …得了, which Taiwan doesn't use. Learners underuse 乾脆 and say 不如 for everything.

examples.zh: 等公車要二十分鐘，乾脆用走的好了。
examples.en: The bus is twenty minutes away; we might as well walk.

examples.zh: 修理這麼貴，乾脆買一台新的。
examples.en: Repairs cost this much — might as well buy a new one.

examples.zh: 既然都來了，乾脆多住一天。
examples.en: Since we're already here, we might as well stay one more day.

examples.zh: 他做事很乾脆，不會拖拖拉拉。
examples.en: He's decisive and doesn't drag things out.

practice.en: It's already so late; you might as well stay over.
practice.zh: 都這麼晚了，你乾脆住下來好了。

practice.en: If you don't like it, just don't go.
practice.zh: 不喜歡的話，乾脆不要去。

title: 難道 — rhetorical 'surely not? / could it be?'
pattern: 難道 + clause + (嗎)？ ; 該不會 … 吧？
explanation: 難道 opens a rhetorical question that expects 'surely not' or voices a dawning suspicion ('don't tell me…'). It goes before or after the subject and usually ends in 嗎. In casual Taiwan speech 該不會…吧 often replaces it for the suspicion sense.
contrast: It is not a neutral question — don't use it simply to ask for information. ✗ 難道 with a wh-question word.

examples.zh: 難道你不知道今天要交報告嗎？
examples.en: Don't you know the report is due today?

examples.zh: 他到現在還沒來，難道是忘了？
examples.en: He still isn't here — could he have forgotten?

examples.zh: 難道就沒有別的辦法了嗎？
examples.en: Is there really no other way?

examples.zh: 你該不會又忘記帶錢包了吧？
examples.en: Don't tell me you forgot your wallet again?

practice.en: Do you really think I don't care?
practice.zh: 難道你覺得我不在乎嗎？

practice.en: Could it be that he already knows?
practice.zh: 難道他已經知道了？

title: 導致 / 造成 / 致使 / 以致 — negative causation
pattern: cause + 導致/造成/致使 + (bad) result ; …，以致 (於) + result clause
explanation: These mark negative causation in formal writing. 造成 takes a noun result (造成損失, 造成不便); 導致 takes a noun or clause (導致交通中斷); 致使 + clause is more literary. 以致 / 以致於 is a conjunction introducing the unfortunate consequence of the preceding clause.
contrast: Spoken: 害 / 讓 / 結果. Don't use these for good results (use 使 / 促成 / 帶來). 以致 (bad result) ≠ 以至 (extent: 'up to, even').

examples.zh: 連日豪雨造成多處道路坍方。
examples.en: Days of torrential rain caused landslides on many roads.

examples.zh: 駕駛疲勞是導致這起車禍的主因。
examples.en: Driver fatigue was the main cause of this car accident.

examples.zh: 施工期間造成不便，敬請見諒。
examples.en: We apologize for any inconvenience caused during construction.

examples.zh: 他長期熬夜，以致健康出了問題。
examples.en: He stayed up late for a long time, with the result that his health suffered.

practice.en: The power outage caused the trains to be delayed.
practice.zh: 停電導致列車誤點。

practice.en: The typhoon caused serious agricultural losses.
practice.zh: 颱風造成嚴重的農業損失。

title: 隨著 — 'as / along with (a change)'
pattern: 隨著 + N (的 + V)，… 越來越 / 逐漸 / 也 …
explanation: 隨著 links a gradual change to the trend behind it. The main clause typically has 越來越, 逐漸 or 也. Neutral-to-formal; a standard opening for essays and news paragraphs.
contrast: 隨著 needs a noun phrase, not a finished clause (✗ 隨著科技發展了). It is not 跟著 ('follow physically / right after').

examples.zh: 隨著年紀增加，他越來越注重健康。
examples.en: As he gets older, he pays more and more attention to his health.

examples.zh: 隨著科技的進步，生活變得更方便。
examples.en: With advances in technology, life has become more convenient.

examples.zh: 隨著物價上漲，外食族的負擔也加重。
examples.en: As prices rise, the burden on people who eat out also grows.

practice.en: As time passed, he gradually got used to it.
practice.zh: 隨著時間過去，他漸漸習慣了。

practice.en: As smartphones became common, fewer and fewer people buy cameras.
practice.zh: 隨著手機普及，買相機的人越來越少。

title: 有 + Adj — 'it really is / is it any …?'
pattern: 有 + (比較 / 這麼 / 那麼) + Adj (+ 嗎) ; 沒有 + Adj
explanation: Taiwan Mandarin lets 有 precede adjectives to assert or question that a quality really holds or has changed: 有比較好嗎？ 'is it any better?', 有好吃 'it IS tasty', 有這麼誇張嗎？ 'is it really that extreme?'. It answers doubt, like stressed 'is / does' in English.
contrast: Mainland/textbook: 好點兒了嗎？/ 確實好吃 / 至於這麼誇張嗎？ ✗ 有好吃 is rejected in mainland standard usage but normal in Taiwan speech.

examples.zh: 吃了藥以後，喉嚨有比較好嗎？
examples.en: Is your throat any better after taking the medicine?

examples.zh: 我覺得這家有好吃，值得排隊。
examples.en: I think this place really is good; it's worth the line.

examples.zh: 有這麼誇張嗎？不過是遲到五分鐘。
examples.en: Is it really that big a deal? It's only five minutes late.

examples.zh: 換了新枕頭，睡覺有比較舒服。
examples.en: With the new pillow, sleeping really is more comfortable.

practice.en: Is it any cheaper to buy online?
practice.zh: 網路上買有比較便宜嗎？

practice.en: Is it really that cold?
practice.zh: 有那麼冷嗎？

title: 是否 / 如何 / 為何 / 何時 — formal question words
pattern: 是否 + V (= …不… / …嗎) ; 如何 (= 怎麼 / 怎麼樣) ; 為何 (= 為什麼) ; 何時 / 何處
explanation: Formal writing swaps colloquial question words for classical ones: 是否 'whether' (是否參加), 如何 'how' (如何解決), 為何 'why', 何時 'when', 何處 'where', 能否 / 可否 'can … or not'. They appear in headlines, forms, emails and embedded questions.
contrast: Spoken: 要不要 / 怎麼 / 為什麼 / 什麼時候. ✗ 是否…嗎 (double question marking). Sentence-final 如何 = 怎麼樣 (結果如何？).

examples.zh: 請於週五前回覆是否出席。
examples.en: Please reply by Friday as to whether you will attend.

examples.zh: 如何兼顧工作與家庭，是許多人的難題。
examples.en: How to balance work and family is a difficult question for many.

examples.zh: 目前仍不清楚火災為何發生。
examples.en: It remains unclear why the fire broke out.

examples.zh: 捷運新路線何時通車，市府尚未確定。
examples.en: The city government has not yet confirmed when the new MRT line will open.

practice.en: Please confirm whether the information is correct.
practice.zh: 請確認資料是否正確。

practice.en: How to reduce plastic waste is an important issue.
practice.zh: 如何減少塑膠垃圾是一個重要的議題。

title: 根據 / 按照 / 依照 — 'according to' vs 'in accordance with'
pattern: 根據 + source/basis，… ; 按照 / 依照 / 依 + rule/plan/order + V ; 照 + V
explanation: 根據 cites the basis of a claim or decision (data, reports, law). 按照 means following a standard, plan or sequence; 依照 / 依 is its more formal version, favored in Taiwan regulations and notices. 照 alone is the spoken short form (照你說的做).
contrast: ✗ 按照新聞報導 (a source → 根據). ✗ 根據他說 → 根據他的說法. Mainland notices use 按 / 按照; Taiwan official text prefers 依 / 依照 / 依規定.

examples.zh: 根據氣象預報，明天會有午後雷陣雨。
examples.en: According to the forecast, there will be afternoon thundershowers tomorrow.

examples.zh: 請按照說明書的步驟安裝。
examples.en: Please install it following the steps in the manual.

examples.zh: 違規停車將依照規定開罰。
examples.en: Illegal parking will be fined in accordance with regulations.

examples.zh: 就照你說的做吧，我沒意見。
examples.en: Let's do it the way you said; I have no objection.

practice.en: According to the survey, most people support this plan.
practice.zh: 根據調查，大部分的人支持這個計畫。

practice.en: Please line up in order.
practice.zh: 請按照順序排隊。

title: 其 — formal 'its / his / their'
pattern: 其 + N (= 他的 / 它的 / 他們的) ; 其中 / 其餘 / 其次
explanation: 其 is the written third-person possessive and demonstrative: 其原因 'its cause', 其家屬 'his or her family'. It refers back to something just mentioned and keeps formal sentences compact. Related words: 其中 'among them', 其餘 'the rest', 其次 'secondly'.
contrast: Spoken: 他的 / 它的 / 那個. ✗ 其 as a subject (✗ 其很重要) — it only modifies a noun or serves as object in set phrases (任其發展).

examples.zh: 該公司宣佈裁員，其原因尚未說明。
examples.en: The company announced layoffs; the reason has not yet been explained.

examples.zh: 這款手機很受歡迎，其價格卻不便宜。
examples.en: This phone is very popular, yet its price is not cheap.

examples.zh: 報名者共兩百人，其中一半是學生。
examples.en: There were 200 applicants in total, half of whom were students.

examples.zh: 警方已通知其家屬到場。
examples.en: The police have notified his family to come to the scene.

practice.en: Every plan has its advantages and disadvantages.
practice.zh: 每個方案都有其優缺點。

practice.en: There are five candidates, three of whom are women.
practice.zh: 候選人共五位，其中三位是女性。

title: 何況 vs 況且 — 'let alone' vs 'besides'
pattern: (連) A 都…，(更) 何況 B ; …，況且 + additional reason
explanation: 何況 is rhetorical: if A is so, B is even more obviously so ('let alone, not to mention'). 況且 adds a further supporting reason ('besides, moreover'). Both are fairly formal; in speech Taiwanese say 更不用說 and 而且 / 再說.
contrast: Learners swap the two. 何況 builds an a fortiori argument (often after 連…都); 況且 only adds a reason. 更何況 can do either.

examples.zh: 連大人都搬不動，何況是小孩？
examples.en: Even adults can't lift it, let alone a child.

examples.zh: 平日都要排隊，更何況是假日。
examples.en: You have to queue even on weekdays, never mind holidays.

examples.zh: 這間套房太小，況且離公司也很遠。
examples.en: This studio is too small, and besides, it's far from the office.

examples.zh: 時間不夠，況且預算也有限。
examples.en: There isn't enough time, and moreover the budget is limited.

practice.en: I can't even afford rent, let alone a house.
practice.zh: 我連房租都付不起，更何況買房子。

practice.en: It's already late; besides, it's raining outside.
practice.zh: 已經很晚了，況且外面在下雨。

title: 則 — 'whereas' and 'then'
pattern: A …，B 則 … (contrast) ; 若/如 …，則 … (consequence) ; 一則 + 新聞/留言
explanation: 則 has two main written uses: marking a contrast between parallel topics ('for its part, whereas': 北部多雨，南部則乾燥) and marking the consequence of a condition ('then': 若有疑問，則…). It sits after the subject of the second clause. As a measure word it counts news items and messages.
contrast: Spoken: 就 / …的話就 / 而. Learners put 則 before the subject (✗ 則南部乾燥).

examples.zh: 北部今天多雲，南部則是晴朗的好天氣。
examples.en: The north is cloudy today, while the south has fine, sunny weather.

examples.zh: 大人票價三百元，兒童則免費入場。
examples.en: Adult tickets are NT$300, while children enter free.

examples.zh: 如未在期限內繳費，則視同放棄。
examples.en: Failure to pay within the deadline will be deemed a forfeit.

examples.zh: 這則新聞在網路上引起熱烈討論。
examples.en: This news item sparked heated discussion online.

practice.en: Some people support it, while others have reservations.
practice.zh: 有些人支持，有些人則持保留態度。

practice.en: If it rains, the event will be moved indoors.
practice.zh: 若遇雨天，活動則改在室內舉行。

title: 都馬 — 'always, as a matter of fact'
pattern: S + 都馬 + VP
explanation: 都馬 (from Taiwanese lóng-mā) is an emphatic 都 for stating what is always true, usually to correct someone's assumption or to complain: 我都馬自己煮 'I always cook myself, actually'. Very colloquial and very Taiwanese; common in speech and chat, never in formal writing.
contrast: Mainland: 都是 / 一直都 / 明明都是. No exact equivalent; recognize it first, then use it in casual talk for the 'actually, it's always…' rebuttal.

examples.zh: 我都馬自己帶便當，很少吃外面。
examples.en: I always bring my own lunch box; I rarely eat out.

examples.zh: 他都馬這樣，講了也不會改。
examples.en: He's always like that; telling him won't change anything.

examples.zh: 都馬是你一直催，我才會忘記帶。
examples.en: It's because you kept rushing me that I forgot to bring it.

examples.zh: 大家都馬用 LINE 聯絡，誰還在打電話？
examples.en: Everyone uses LINE to keep in touch — who still makes calls?

practice.en: I always take the MRT to work, actually.
practice.zh: 我都馬搭捷運上班。

practice.en: You always say that.
practice.zh: 你都馬這樣講。

title: 以免 / 免得 / 省得 vs 以便 — negative and positive purpose
pattern: …，以免 / 免得 / 省得 + unwanted result ; …，以便 + intended result
explanation: 以免 and 免得 introduce what an action is meant to avoid ('so as not to, lest'): 以免 is written and found on signs, 免得 is spoken. 省得 means 'saving the trouble of'. 以便 is the positive counterpart in formal style: 'so that … can'.
contrast: Mainland speech uses 省得 freely; in Taiwan 免得 or 才不會 is more usual (早點出門才不會遲到). Don't put 不 after 以免 (✗ 以免不遲到).

examples.zh: 請提早出門，以免錯過班機。
examples.en: Please leave early so as not to miss your flight.

examples.zh: 你先打電話問一下，免得白跑一趟。
examples.en: Call and ask first so you don't make the trip for nothing.

examples.zh: 我直接傳給你，省得你再找。
examples.en: I'll send it straight to you to save you looking for it.

examples.zh: 請留下聯絡電話，以便我們通知您。
examples.en: Please leave a contact number so that we can notify you.

practice.en: Write it down so you don't forget.
practice.zh: 你寫下來，免得忘記。

practice.en: Please arrive ten minutes early so as not to delay the meeting.
practice.zh: 請提早十分鐘到，以免耽誤會議。

title: 即 — formal 就 (即可、即將、亦即)
pattern: A 即 B (= 就是) ; V1 + 即 + V2 (= 就) ; 即可 / 即將 / 立即 / 亦即
explanation: 即 is the written 就: 'is precisely' (此即問題所在), 'then, right away' (用畢即丟) and part of many formal words: 即將 'about to', 即可 'will suffice', 立即 'at once', 亦即 'that is'. 即可 is everywhere in Taiwan instructions.
contrast: Spoken: 就是 / 就可以了 / 馬上. Learners write 就可以 in formal instructions where 即可 is expected.

examples.zh: 掃描 QR Code 即可完成報名。
examples.en: Simply scan the QR code to complete registration.

examples.zh: 新制度即將上路，請民眾多加留意。
examples.en: The new system is about to take effect; the public is asked to take note.

examples.zh: 加熱三分鐘即可食用。
examples.en: Heat for three minutes and it is ready to eat.

examples.zh: 所謂通膨，即物價持續上漲的現象。
examples.en: Inflation is the phenomenon of prices rising continuously.

practice.en: Simply show your student ID to get the discount.
practice.zh: 出示學生證即可享有優惠。

practice.en: The typhoon is about to make landfall.
practice.zh: 颱風即將登陸。

title: 啊 as a sentence opener — 'so… / and… / but…'
pattern: 啊 + 你/就/不是/後來 + clause
explanation: An unstressed 啊 at the very start of a sentence comes from Taiwanese and works as a casual linker: 啊你呢？ 'and you?'; 啊就… introduces an obvious or reluctant explanation; 啊你不是說… points out a contradiction. Homey and informal, typical of family talk and southern speech.
contrast: Mainland: 那你呢？/ 不是說…嗎？ with no opener. Don't confuse it with exclamatory 啊！ — the opener is short, flat and attached to the next word.

examples.zh: 我要回家了，啊你呢？
examples.en: I'm heading home. And you?

examples.zh: 啊你不是說今天要加班？
examples.en: Wait, didn't you say you were working late today?

examples.zh: 啊就很忙啊，哪有時間運動。
examples.en: Well, I'm just busy — where would I find time to exercise?

examples.zh: 啊你們吃飽了沒？
examples.en: So, have you guys eaten yet?

practice.en: And then what happened?
practice.zh: 啊後來咧？

practice.en: But didn't you say you don't eat spicy food?
practice.zh: 啊你不是說你不吃辣？

title: 所以說 / 反正就是 — getting to the point
pattern: 所以說 (嘛)，… ; 反正就是 …
explanation: 所以說 draws the moral of what was just discussed ('so you see', 'which is why'), sometimes with an I-told-you-so tone. 反正就是 cuts through the details to the bottom line ('anyway, the point is'). Both help you wrap up a story or steer back to the main point.
contrast: 總之 does this job in writing; in Taiwan conversation 反正就是 and 所以說 do the work. Don't open a reply with 所以說 to a superior — it can sound like a lecture.

examples.zh: 所以說，出門前一定要先查天氣。
examples.en: So you see, you really have to check the weather before going out.

examples.zh: 所以說嘛，便宜的東西不一定划算。
examples.en: That's why I say cheap things aren't necessarily a bargain.

examples.zh: 反正就是我搞錯時間，白跑一趟。
examples.en: Anyway, bottom line: I got the time wrong and made the trip for nothing.

examples.zh: 細節我忘了，反正就是他不來了。
examples.en: I forget the details; the point is he's not coming.

practice.en: So that's why you should always back up your files.
practice.zh: 所以說，檔案一定要備份。

practice.en: Anyway, the point is we need more time.
practice.zh: 反正就是我們需要更多時間。

title: 難免 — 'bound to, can't be helped'
pattern: (S) 難免 (會/有) + V/Adj ; …是難免的
explanation: 難免 means 'hard to avoid', used to excuse or normalize an imperfect outcome. It usually comes with 會 or 有, and …是難免的 works as a comforting conclusion. 免不了 is the more colloquial variant.
contrast: 難免 ≠ 未必, and it isn't used for good outcomes. 不免 is more literary and only precedes affirmative verbs.

examples.zh: 第一次上台，難免會緊張。
examples.en: It's your first time on stage; being nervous is only natural.

examples.zh: 剛到新環境，難免有點不習慣。
examples.en: Having just arrived in a new environment, feeling a bit unsettled is inevitable.

examples.zh: 人多的地方難免會有摩擦。
examples.en: Where there are lots of people, friction is bound to occur.

examples.zh: 做生意有賺有賠是難免的。
examples.en: In business, both gains and losses are unavoidable.

practice.en: Everyone is bound to make mistakes sometimes.
practice.zh: 每個人難免都會犯錯。

practice.en: Living abroad, it's natural to feel homesick.
practice.zh: 住在國外，難免會想家。

title: 為…所 — the literary passive
pattern: 為 + agent + 所 + V
explanation: 為…所 is the classical-style passive of formal writing: 為人所知 'known to people', 為生活所迫 'forced by circumstances'. It is common in four-character-style phrases and in essays that want to avoid repeating 被.
contrast: Spoken: 被 + agent + V. The verb is usually a fixed or two-syllable item and takes no 了; don't use it for casual events (✗ 為老闆所罵).

examples.zh: 這位作家的作品廣為讀者所喜愛。
examples.en: This writer's works are widely loved by readers.

examples.zh: 他不為金錢所動，堅持自己的原則。
examples.en: Unmoved by money, he holds to his principles.

examples.zh: 這個小鎮過去鮮為人所知。
examples.en: This small town was little known in the past.

examples.zh: 許多人為生活所迫，不得不離鄉工作。
examples.en: Forced by circumstances, many people have to leave home to work.

practice.en: This fact is known to few people.
practice.zh: 這個事實鮮為人所知。

practice.en: We should not be swayed by rumors.
practice.zh: 我們不應為謠言所影響。

title: 鑑於 / 有鑑於此 / 基於 — 'in view of' and 'on the basis of'
pattern: 鑑於 / 有鑑於 + situation，… ; 有鑑於此，… ; 基於 + reason/principle，…
explanation: 鑑於 / 有鑑於 means 'in view of' an observed situation that motivates a decision; 有鑑於此 ('in view of this') opens the sentence that announces the response. 基於 means 'on the basis of / out of' a principle or consideration (基於安全考量). All are official-register.
contrast: Spoken: 因為 / 考慮到. Taiwan writes 鑑 (not 鑒). ✗ 基於 for evidence — that is 根據.

examples.zh: 鑑於疫情升溫，主辦單位決定取消活動。
examples.en: In view of the worsening outbreak, the organizers decided to cancel the event.

examples.zh: 有鑑於此，教育部將修訂相關規定。
examples.en: In view of this, the Ministry of Education will revise the relevant rules.

examples.zh: 基於安全考量，頂樓暫不開放。
examples.en: For safety reasons, the rooftop is temporarily closed.

examples.zh: 基於個資保護，本公司無法提供名單。
examples.en: For reasons of personal data protection, our company cannot provide the list.

practice.en: For safety reasons, please do not use the elevator.
practice.zh: 基於安全考量，請勿使用電梯。

practice.en: In view of the heavy rain, classes are suspended today.
practice.zh: 鑑於雨勢過大，今日停止上課。

title: 無非 / 不外乎 — 'nothing more than / comes down to'
pattern: 無非 (是) + … ; 不外乎 (是) + A、B (、C)
explanation: Both reduce something to its essentials: 無非 = 'nothing but, simply' (often revealing a motive); 不外乎 = 'comes down to', usually followed by a short list. Formal-leaning; common in commentary and essays.
contrast: Spoken equivalents: 只不過是 / 就是…而已 / 不就是. Don't follow 無非 with a negative verb.

examples.zh: 父母這麼嘮叨，無非是擔心你。
examples.en: Parents nag like this simply because they worry about you.

examples.zh: 他這麼說，無非是想推卸責任。
examples.en: He says this for no other reason than to dodge responsibility.

examples.zh: 失敗的原因不外乎準備不足。
examples.en: The cause of failure basically comes down to insufficient preparation.

examples.zh: 上班族的煩惱不外乎錢和時間。
examples.en: Office workers' worries boil down to money and time.

practice.en: He did this simply to get attention.
practice.zh: 他這麼做，無非是想引起注意。

practice.en: People's reasons for changing jobs come down to salary and environment.
practice.zh: 換工作的理由不外乎薪水和環境。

title: …的啦 / …的說 — reassuring and afterthought endings
pattern: clause + 的啦 ; clause + 的說
explanation: 的啦 adds casual reassurance or insistence ('it'll be fine, really'). 的說 is a chatty afterthought ending that marks mild surprise, regret or contradiction ('…and here I thought'). Both are informal and common in LINE messages; use 的說 sparingly.
contrast: No mainland equivalent for 的說 (roughly …來著 / …呢); plain 的 or nothing would be used. Overusing 的說 sounds childish.

examples.zh: 不用擔心，一定會過的啦。
examples.en: Don't worry, you'll definitely pass.

examples.zh: 沒關係的啦，下次再約就好。
examples.en: It's really fine; we'll just meet next time.

examples.zh: 我本來想請你吃飯的說。
examples.en: And here I was going to treat you to a meal.

examples.zh: 這家以前很好吃的說，怎麼變了？
examples.en: This place used to be really good — what happened?

practice.en: It'll be fine, really.
practice.zh: 不會有事的啦。

practice.en: I thought you were coming, though.
practice.zh: 我以為你會來的說。

title: 加以 / 予以 / 給予 — formal 'dummy' verbs
pattern: (對 + O) + 加以 + V ; 予以 + V ; 給予 + N (支持 / 協助 / 肯定)
explanation: These verbs turn an action into a formal verb–object phrase. 加以 means 'subject it to' (加以改善, 加以說明), 予以 means 'officially apply or grant' (予以補助, 予以處分), and 給予 means 'give' an abstract noun (給予支持). The real object comes earlier, after 對 or as the topic.
contrast: Spoken: just the verb (改善 / 幫). ✗ 加以 + one-syllable verb (✗ 加以改) or with the object after it (✗ 加以改善這個問題 → 對這個問題加以改善).

examples.zh: 對於民眾反映的問題，市府將加以改善。
examples.en: The city government will address the problems raised by the public.

examples.zh: 違反規定者，將依法予以處分。
examples.en: Violators will be penalized in accordance with the law.

examples.zh: 感謝各位一直以來給予的支持。
examples.en: Thank you all for the support you have given all along.

examples.zh: 這些資料必須加以整理後才能使用。
examples.en: These materials must be sorted out before they can be used.

practice.en: The government should give these families more assistance.
practice.zh: 政府應給予這些家庭更多協助。

practice.en: These problems must be discussed further.
practice.zh: 這些問題必須進一步加以討論。

title: 固然…但 — 'admittedly… but'
pattern: A 固然 + Adj/V，但(是) / 卻 / 不過 + B
explanation: 固然 fully grants a point before introducing a more important consideration. It sounds measured and is a staple of argumentative essays. 固然 follows the subject.
contrast: Unlike 雖然, 固然 can't start the sentence before the subject. The spoken Taiwan equivalent is …是…啦，可是… (便宜是便宜啦，可是…).

examples.zh: 成績固然重要，但健康更重要。
examples.en: Grades are certainly important, but health matters more.

examples.zh: 這個方法固然可行，但成本太高。
examples.en: This method is admittedly workable, but the cost is too high.

examples.zh: 網路固然方便，卻也帶來不少問題。
examples.en: The internet is certainly convenient, yet it also brings quite a few problems.

practice.en: Money is admittedly important, but it isn't everything.
practice.zh: 錢固然重要，但不是一切。

practice.en: Experience certainly matters, but attitude matters more.
practice.zh: 經驗固然重要，但態度更重要。

title: 從而 / 進而 — 'thereby' and 'and then go on to'
pattern: …，從而 + result ; …，進而 + further step
explanation: 從而 links a method or cause to the result it brings about ('thereby'). 進而 introduces a further stage that builds on the first ('and in turn'). Both follow a complete first clause and share its subject; they are staples of analytical writing.
contrast: Spoken: 這樣就… / 然後還…. ✗ 從而 with a new subject or after an unrelated clause. 因而 = 'therefore' (pure cause); 進而 = progression.

examples.zh: 多閱讀可以增加詞彙量，從而提升寫作能力。
examples.en: Reading more can expand vocabulary, thereby improving writing ability.

examples.zh: 政府希望降低稅率，從而刺激消費。
examples.en: The government hopes to lower tax rates and thereby stimulate consumption.

examples.zh: 先瞭解問題的原因，進而找出解決方法。
examples.en: First understand the cause of the problem, then go on to find a solution.

examples.zh: 壓力過大會影響睡眠，進而損害健康。
examples.en: Excessive stress affects sleep and in turn damages health.

practice.en: Exercise reduces stress and thereby improves work efficiency.
practice.zh: 運動可以減輕壓力，從而提高工作效率。

practice.en: We should first build mutual trust and then deepen cooperation.
practice.zh: 我們應先建立互信，進而深化合作。

title: 甚至 / 乃至 — 'even' and 'and even as far as'
pattern: …，甚至 (連) … ; A、B 乃至 (於) C
explanation: 甚至 escalates to a more extreme case ('even, go so far as to') and is used in both speech and writing. 乃至 / 乃至於 is literary and typically closes a widening list: 個人、家庭乃至整個社會.
contrast: Spoken Taiwan: 甚至 / 連…都. 乃至 is written only. ✗ 甚至 before the first item of a list.

examples.zh: 他忙到沒時間吃飯，甚至連水都忘了喝。
examples.en: He was too busy to eat, and even forgot to drink water.

examples.zh: 有些人甚至願意排隊三個小時。
examples.en: Some people are even willing to queue for three hours.

examples.zh: 這項技術將影響台灣乃至全球的產業。
examples.en: This technology will affect industry in Taiwan and even worldwide.

examples.zh: 少子化衝擊學校、企業乃至整個社會。
examples.en: The falling birthrate is hitting schools, businesses and even society as a whole.

practice.en: Some people don't even know who their neighbors are.
practice.zh: 有些人甚至不知道鄰居是誰。

practice.en: This issue concerns individuals, families and even the whole country.
practice.zh: 這個議題關係到個人、家庭乃至整個國家。

title: 恨不得 / 巴不得 — 'wish I could' and 'can't wait for'
pattern: 恨不得 + (unrealizable) VP ; 巴不得 + (hoped-for) clause
explanation: 恨不得 expresses an intense wish to do something that isn't actually possible right now ('I wish I could just…'). 巴不得 is an eager wish for something that could well happen ('would love nothing more than'). Both are vivid, spoken and slightly dramatic.
contrast: 恨不得 has nothing to do with hating. ✗ 恨不得 with an ordinary realizable plan (use 很想). The standalone reply 我巴不得呢 is mainland; in Taiwan say 求之不得.

examples.zh: 我恨不得現在就飛回台灣。
examples.en: I wish I could fly back to Taiwan right this minute.

examples.zh: 當時好丟臉，恨不得找個洞鑽進去。
examples.en: It was so embarrassing I wished I could crawl into a hole.

examples.zh: 他巴不得明天就放暑假。
examples.en: He can't wait for summer vacation to start tomorrow.

examples.zh: 她巴不得你趕快離職。
examples.en: She'd love nothing more than for you to quit soon.

practice.en: I wish I could quit right now.
practice.zh: 我恨不得現在就辭職。

practice.en: He'd love for the meeting to be cancelled.
practice.zh: 他巴不得會議取消。

title: 捏 / 餒 — cutesy chat spellings of 耶 / 呢
pattern: clause + 捏 / 餒
explanation: In messages and cutesy speech, 耶 and 呢 are respelled 捏 or 餒 to sound playful, hesitant or sweet: 不知道捏, 好可愛捏. Internet-flavored and mostly used by younger speakers in LINE, Dcard and Instagram captions. Recognize it; use it only in very casual chat.
contrast: Standard spelling: 不知道耶 / 好可愛喔. Never use it in work email or essays, and note that it can read as overly cute from someone you don't know well.

examples.zh: 我也不知道捏，你問他看看。
examples.en: I dunno either~ try asking him.

examples.zh: 這隻貓好可愛捏！
examples.en: This cat is sooo cute!

examples.zh: 今天有點懶，不太想出門捏。
examples.en: Feeling a bit lazy today; don't really wanna go out~

practice.en: Hmm, I'm not sure~ (cute, in chat)
practice.zh: 我不太確定捏。

practice.en: It looks really yummy~ (cute, in chat)
practice.zh: 看起來好好吃捏。

title: 你知道嗎 / 你懂我意思嗎 — pulling the listener in
pattern: 你知道嗎，… ; …，你知道嗎？ ; 你懂我意思嗎？
explanation: 你知道嗎 hooks the listener before surprising news; tacked on at the end it seeks empathy ('you know?'). 你懂我意思嗎 checks that a hard-to-express point landed. Used with feeling they make storytelling sound native; overused they become a verbal tic.
contrast: Mainland: 你明白我意思吧 / 你造嗎 (slang). Don't say 你懂嗎 to superiors — it sounds condescending; use 不知道我這樣講清不清楚.

examples.zh: 你知道嗎，他們兩個居然在一起了。
examples.en: You know what? Those two actually got together.

examples.zh: 我真的很努力了，你知道嗎？
examples.en: I really did try my best, you know?

examples.zh: 就是那種很悶的感覺，你懂我意思嗎？
examples.en: It's that kind of stifling feeling — you know what I mean?

practice.en: You know what? I ran into our teacher on the MRT today.
practice.zh: 你知道嗎，我今天在捷運上遇到老師。

practice.en: It's really tiring, you know?
practice.zh: 真的很累，你知道嗎？

title: 值得一提的是 / 值得注意的是 — highlighting a point
pattern: 值得一提 / 值得注意 的是，+ clause ; 更重要的是，… ; 不可否認的是，…
explanation: These sentence openers highlight a point: 值得一提的是 adds a notable extra; 值得注意的是 flags something the reader should weigh. The same frame gives 更重要的是, 令人意外的是 and 不可否認的是.
contrast: Spoken: 對了 / 還有一點 / 重點是. Learners who want 'by the way' in an essay should use these, not 順便說.

examples.zh: 值得一提的是，這部電影全程在台南拍攝。
examples.en: It is worth mentioning that this film was shot entirely in Tainan.

examples.zh: 值得注意的是，年輕族群的投票率明顯上升。
examples.en: Notably, turnout among young voters rose markedly.

examples.zh: 更重要的是，這項改變並不需要額外經費。
examples.en: More importantly, this change requires no additional funding.

examples.zh: 不可否認的是，科技也帶來了新的問題。
examples.en: It cannot be denied that technology has also brought new problems.

practice.en: It is worth mentioning that all the staff are volunteers.
practice.zh: 值得一提的是，所有工作人員都是志工。

practice.en: It is worth noting that prices are still rising.
practice.zh: 值得注意的是，物價仍持續上漲。

title: 何必 / 何苦 — 'why bother?'
pattern: 何必 + V (呢)？ ; 何苦 (呢)？ / 何苦 + V
explanation: 何必 asks rhetorically why someone bothers: 'there's no need to…'. 何苦 adds that the person is only making themselves suffer. Both are gentle, somewhat literary ways to advise against something. Spoken Taiwan equivalents: 幹嘛 / 不用 / 沒必要.
contrast: 何必 ≠ 何不 ('why not', a suggestion). Mainland 犯不著 isn't used in Taiwan.

examples.zh: 都是小事，何必這麼生氣呢？
examples.en: It's a trivial thing — why get so angry?

examples.zh: 既然不喜歡，何必勉強自己？
examples.en: If you don't like it, why force yourself?

examples.zh: 為了這種人難過，何苦呢？
examples.en: Being upset over a person like that — why do that to yourself?

examples.zh: 捷運五分鐘就到，何必搭計程車？
examples.en: The MRT gets there in five minutes — why take a taxi?

practice.en: It's only a few dollars; why make a fuss?
practice.zh: 才幾塊錢，何必計較？

practice.en: It's all in the past; why torment yourself?
practice.zh: 事情都過去了，何苦折磨自己？

title: 啊不然咧 / 不然咧 — 'well, what else?'
pattern: (啊) 不然咧？ ; 不然要怎麼辦？
explanation: A rhetorical comeback meaning 'obviously — what did you expect?' or 'what's the alternative?'. With the Taiwanese-style opener 啊 and final 咧 it sounds cheeky: playful among friends, rude to strangers or superiors. 不然要怎麼辦 is the resigned, non-sassy version.
contrast: Mainland: 那不然呢？/ 要不然呢？/ 那還能怎樣？ The 啊…咧 packaging is distinctly Taiwanese.

examples.zh: 你又吃泡麵喔？——啊不然咧，我沒錢了。
examples.en: Instant noodles again? — Well, what else? I'm broke.

examples.zh: 你真的要自己搬？——不然咧？
examples.en: You're really moving it yourself? — What else would I do?

examples.zh: 只能等了，不然要怎麼辦？
examples.en: All we can do is wait — what else is there?

practice.en: You're working on Saturday? — Well, what choice do I have?
practice.zh: 你禮拜六要上班喔？——啊不然咧？

practice.en: We'll just have to redo it. What else can we do?
practice.zh: 只好重做了，不然要怎麼辦？

title: 換言之 / 也就是說 / 簡言之 — restating
pattern: …。換言之 / 也就是說 / 簡言之，+ restatement
explanation: 換言之 ('in other words') restates a point more plainly or draws out its implication; 也就是說 is the neutral equivalent that also works in speech; 簡言之 / 簡單來說 means 'in short'. They tell the reader you are clarifying, not adding.
contrast: Spoken: 就是說 / 意思就是. ✗ Writing 換言之 and then saying something new rather than a paraphrase.

examples.zh: 出生率持續下降，換言之，勞動力將越來越少。
examples.en: The birthrate keeps falling; in other words, the workforce will keep shrinking.

examples.zh: 他沒有回覆，也就是說他不打算參加。
examples.en: He didn't reply, which is to say he doesn't intend to take part.

examples.zh: 簡言之，這項計畫的成本遠高於效益。
examples.en: In short, the costs of this plan far exceed the benefits.

practice.en: In other words, we have to start over.
practice.zh: 換言之，我們必須重新開始。

practice.en: That is to say, the deadline is this Friday.
practice.zh: 也就是說，期限是這個禮拜五。

title: 不妨 — 'there's no harm in / you might'
pattern: (S) 不妨 + V (+ 看看 / 一下)
explanation: 不妨 makes a polite, low-pressure suggestion. It suits advice columns, customer service and courteous speech, and often pairs with 試試, 考慮, 參考. The spoken equivalent is 可以…看看.
contrast: Learners overuse 應該, which sounds like an obligation. Don't use 不妨 for urgent or serious advice.

examples.zh: 有空的話，不妨去那家店看看。
examples.en: If you have time, you might drop by that shop.

examples.zh: 如果睡不著，不妨試試聽輕音樂。
examples.en: If you can't sleep, try listening to some soft music.

examples.zh: 遇到問題時，不妨先問問同事。
examples.en: When you hit a problem, there's no harm in asking a coworker first.

practice.en: You might consider a different approach.
practice.zh: 你不妨考慮換個方法。

practice.en: If you're interested, you might sign up and give it a try.
practice.zh: 有興趣的話，不妨報名試試看。

title: 總而言之 / 綜上所述 / 由此可見 — concluding and inferring
pattern: 總而言之 / 總之 / 綜上所述，+ conclusion ; 由此可見 / 由此可知，+ inference
explanation: 總而言之 and 總之 ('in sum') wrap up an argument; 綜上所述 ('in light of the above') is the classic essay-conclusion opener. 由此可見 / 由此可知 draws an inference from evidence just presented. Such signposts are expected in TOCFL and HSK 6 essays.
contrast: Spoken: 反正 / 所以說. ✗ 由此可見 with no evidence before it. Don't conclude an argument with 最後 alone.

examples.zh: 總而言之，這次活動算是相當成功。
examples.en: All in all, this event can be considered quite successful.

examples.zh: 綜上所述，遠距工作利大於弊。
examples.en: In light of the above, the benefits of remote work outweigh the drawbacks.

examples.zh: 由此可見，飲食習慣對健康影響很大。
examples.en: From this it is clear that eating habits greatly affect health.

examples.zh: 總之，我們需要更多時間來評估。
examples.en: In short, we need more time to evaluate.

practice.en: In sum, there is no perfect answer to this question.
practice.zh: 總而言之，這個問題沒有完美的答案。

practice.en: From this we can see that education is very important.
practice.zh: 由此可見，教育非常重要。
